props.title: About Aether
props.description: Aether is a privacy-first student resilience ecosystem that helps students reflect, understand what kind of support fits the moment, and move toward safer next steps without pretending to be therapy or emergency care.

items.label: support modules
items.description: Reflection, check-ins, safety planning, resource routing, and peer connection.

items.label: diagnostic claims
items.description: Aether supports awareness and navigation; it does not diagnose, treat, or replace care.

items.label: privacy posture
items.description: Sensitive reflection experiences are designed around data minimization and local-first patterns.

items.label: deployment model
items.description: Campuses and teams can enable, disable, or swap pathways without rebuilding the product.

props.title: How Aether fits together
props.description: Each capability can stand alone, but the complete system gives students a coherent path from reflection to support.

items.title: Echo Chamber
items.description: A private voice reflection space where students can process stress and receive local sentiment and safety cues without turning reflection into a public record.

items.title: Peer-Navigator
items.description: A privacy-aware matching experience designed to improve belonging while preserving identity safety and fairness review.

items.title: Resilience Pathway
items.description: A modular intervention flow covering check-ins, safety planning, resource routing, peer circles, and sustainable habits.

items.title: Privacy and Governance
items.description: Designed with local-first processing, transparent policy boundaries, and fairness-focused auditability.

props.title: Why Aether exists
props.description: Students often need help before a crisis, but traditional support pathways can feel hard to find, stigmatizing, or too heavy for early stress. Aether fills the space between doing nothing and formal care by making small, responsible next steps easier to reach.

items.title: Lower the first step
items.description: The product starts with low-pressure reflection and simple routing so students can name what is happening before they need a formal appointment.

items.title: Protect dignity
items.description: Aether avoids shame-heavy language, diagnostic labels, and hidden surveillance patterns. The student remains a person, not a risk score.

items.title: Support real handoffs
items.description: The experience points toward peer support, campus services, trusted people, and crisis resources when the situation calls for more than self-guided tools.

props.title: What makes the system safe to reuse
props.description: The About page should make the product boundaries obvious. These principles keep Aether generic enough for many institutions while preserving a serious safety posture.

items.title: Non-clinical by default
items.description: Aether provides education, reflection, and navigation support. It is not a medical device, therapist, counselor, emergency responder, or diagnostic tool.

items.title: Privacy before personalization
items.description: Personalization should come from explicit context and local interactions where possible, not broad collection of sensitive student data.

items.title: Human pathways stay visible
items.description: Crisis support, trusted contacts, campus resources, and peer pathways remain visible instead of being buried behind AI chat or long intake flows.

items.title: Config over rewrites
items.description: Content, resources, page availability, and support pathways are modeled as swappable configuration wherever possible.

props.title: What Aether is and is not
props.description: A clear About page should build trust by saying where the product helps and where it must step aside.

items.title: Aether is a resilience layer
items.description: It helps students reflect, practice coping habits, organize support plans, and find the next appropriate resource.

items.title: Aether is not emergency care
items.description: If someone may be in immediate danger, the right path is local emergency services or a crisis line such as 988 in the United States.

props.title: Next step
props.description: Aether is designed as a humane support layer: practical, privacy-aware, and careful about its limits.
